title: Father's Legacy
next_chapter_hook: The last page of the manual was burned, leaving only half a sentence: The true cost of the Heavenly Fate Lock is...

text.content:
The prophetic shadow of the Tianji Record slowly dissolved before Chen Ji's eyes. That blurry image—a collapsed altar at the convergence of three bloodlines—pierced his heart like a thorn. Moonlight outside the window gleamed like frost, casting the stone cottage in a deathly pale hue. Chen Nian sat across from him, her fingertips unconsciously rubbing the sleeve where she hid a scroll of yellowed silk.

"Brother, there's something I intended to take to my grave." Her voice was soft. "But since the Tianji Record has already manifested... I can no longer hide it from you."

dialogue.content:
This was given to me by our father on his deathbed.

He told me to present it when you truly need it—not when you want to use it, but when you must use it.

text.content:
The moment Chen Ji took the silk scroll, his fingers trembled slightly.

Those were Chen Xuan's calligraphy—vigorous yet hurried, with uneven ink depth, clearly written in an extremely short time. He recognized this handwriting—the same forceful strokes his father used when teaching him to read as a child.

Only back then, Father's characters were always composed and unhurried.

"When did Father give this to you?" His voice turned hoarse.

Chen Nian lowered her eyes: "The night before he was taken. He said, if he didn't make it back, I should give it to you at the appropriate time."

dialogue.content:
I never understood what 'the appropriate time' meant.

Until today, when the Tianji Record manifested that image—three bloodlines converging, the altar collapsing. Only then did I realize that what Father wanted us to see was never an ending, but a beginning.

text.content:
Chen Ji unrolled the manual, dense small characters filling his vision.

「The Three Heavenly Bloodlines were not born separated. Ji'er, Nian'er, Qing'er—you three share the same origin. The Heavenly Eye sensed the hidden danger within our Chen family's bloodline and sought to eradicate us completely. To protect you, I had no choice but to separate you—」

Chen Ji's breath caught abruptly.

Same origin? The three bloodlines reuniting actually referred to the three of them?

The handwriting in the manual grew increasingly messy, as if the writer was racing against time.

「The Heavenly Eye's assassination plan began thirty years ago. It manipulated the Holy Sect, Xuanwu Sect, even the Tianqing Sect, driving me into a corner. I calculated that if we three gathered in one place, the Heavenly Eye would personally strike. So I chose to separate you willingly—making the pursuers believe the Chen bloodline had been severed.」

The veins on Chen Ji's hand clutching the silk scroll bulged.

Father hadn't abandoned them—he had entered the game himself, using his life to buy them time to survive.

dialogue.content:
Father said the person he wronged the most was you.

He sent you to the Tianqing Sect as a servant, yet couldn't tell you the truth. Because he knew that once you learned of your origins, you would definitely rush to confront the Heavenly Eye.

text.content:
Chen Ji fell silent.

He remembered standing at the sect gate when he was sent to the Tianqing Sect at ten years old, his father's silhouette in the distance. That figure never turned back, only waved goodbye.

He had always thought Father嫌弃 him for his mediocre talent, unwilling to see him again.

So that farewell carried tenderness he never dared to look back upon.

"The clue to the fourth layer of the Tianji Record's seal..." he suddenly spoke, his voice low. "Where is it?"

dialogue.content:
On the manual's last page.

But that part... was burned. Father's writing stopped halfway, the remaining portion erased by some force.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji took a deep breath. Facing his father's unfinished game, what choice would he make?

choices.description: Father's layout must be airtight—the burned section must have a backup plan
choices.risk_hint: Clues may require specific conditions to activate

text.content: Chen Ji held the manual close to the candlelight. Under the side illumination, faint golden characters emerged between the paper fibers—written in another kind of ink, invisible to the naked eye, only appearing under specific light. His pupils contracted slightly: "Father... he left another card."

choices.description: Emotional fluctuations affect judgment—first compose yourself
choices.risk_hint: Time is tight—you might miss the opportunity

dialogue.content:
Brother, you're crying.

Chen Nian reached out, gently wiping away the tear at the corner of Chen Ji's eye. In this moment, she was no longer the girl imprisoned by the Holy Sect for years—just a younger sister heartbroken for her brother.

text.content:
The pale golden characters slowly revealed themselves. Chen Ji held his breath.

「The key to the fourth layer of the seal lies not within the Tianji Record, but in your three hearts. Three bloodlines share the same origin—memory sharing. When you truly understand what 'family' means, the seal will lift itself.」

Chen Ji's gaze flickered slightly.

Father's meaning was... the fourth seal's unlocking condition was actually emotional bonds?

dialogue.content:
I remember now.

Chen Nian suddenly spoke, a dazed light flashing in her eyes. When the Holy Sect imprisoned me, they used a secret technique that made me forget many things. But just now, seeing this line, a scene suddenly emerged in my mind—Father holding the three of us children, teaching us to draw a circle.

text.content:
Chen Ji shuddered all over.

He had similar memory fragments—but those images had always been blurry, like looking through a layer of mist.

Three people... was Ye Qing one of them too?

He suddenly remembered the names on the Tianji Record Fragment: Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Chen Ji. The three names listed side by side, echoing the Three Heavenly Bloodlines from afar.

So from the very beginning, the three of them had been bound by fate.

Father, how far into the future did you actually see?

choice.prompt: Chen Ji held the incomplete manual, his heart churning with complex emotions.

choices.description: The three bloodlines must converge to unseal—this matter cannot be delayed
choices.risk_hint: The Demonic Path Saint's whereabouts are unpredictable—others may notice

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji? I already know about the three bloodlines reuniting.

Ye Qing's voice came through the communication jade talisman, carrying a rare gravity. Does your father's manual mention 'the cost of the Heavenly Fate Lock'?

choices.description: Cannot overlook any details—Father's layout must have profound meaning
choices.risk_hint: Time is tight—the enemy won't wait

text.content:
Chen Ji held the manual close to the candlelight, examining every corner of the paper inch by inch. His gaze suddenly fixed on the back cover of the manual—where there was an extremely faint seal mark, shaped like... a closed eye.

The symbol of the Heavenly Eye.

Why would this appear on Father's legacy?

Ye Qing's words made Chen Ji's heart sink abruptly.

"How do you know those words are on the manual?"

"I don't." Ye Qing's voice rarely carried a tremor. "But just now, at the Demonic Path Holy Sect, I sensed a familiar power fluctuation—that was the aura of the Tianji Record. It... was calling me."

Chen Ji and Chen Nian exchanged glances, both seeing the same speculation in each other's eyes.

The fourth layer of the Tianji Record's seal was probably not just simple unlocking... It involved the Heavenly Eye itself.

"The manual's last page..." Chen Nian suddenly spoke, her voice tight. "It's burning!"

Chen Ji looked down. The edge of the manual's last page was glowing with faint firelight. That flame was no ordinary fire, but an extremely pale gold—identical to the seal's glow on the Tianji Record.

As if some force was actively destroying the final part of this manual.

"The true cost of the Heavenly Fate Lock is..." Chen Nian urgently read the remaining words, her voice growing softer. "Is—!"

Before she could finish, the last page had turned to ash.

Only that half-sentence remained, clearly seared into Chen Ji's mind, heavier than any prophecy.

Father... how deep a road did you pave for us in hell?

dialogue.content:
Brother, I'm not afraid.

Chen Nian's voice was soft, yet exceptionally firm. Whatever the cost, we bear it together.

She raised her head. In the moonlight, her face, bearing five points of resemblance to Chen Ji, carried a stubborn smile. Father separated us so we could survive. Now that we've reunited, we will never part again.

text.content:
Chen Ji was silent for a moment.

Outside the window, the night wind suddenly rose violently, causing the candlelight to flicker unsteadily. He tucked the incomplete manual into his chest, his movements gentle as if cradling some precious, fragile treasure.

Father.

He looked up at the night sky. The confusion in his eyes gradually faded, replaced by a kind of resolve.

The road you paved, I will walk to its end. The words you didn't get to say, I will speak directly to the Heavenly Eye.

A Chen family member never owes a debt.

He turned to look at Chen Nian, his voice low: "Let's go find Ye Qing. The three bloodlines reuniting... it's time."

In the moonlight, the youth's back was no longer frail. On his shoulders he carried his father's legacy; in his chest he bore fate's riddle; and the path ahead—slowly unfolded.

Only that half-burned sentence hung like a sword above his head, ready to fall at any moment.

What exactly was the true cost of the Heavenly Fate Lock...?

dialogue.content:
Chen Nian, call me brother one more time.

He suddenly spoke, the corners of his mouth lifting slightly, carrying a warmth he hadn't felt in so long. This time, it wasn't a life-or-death moment—he simply wanted to hear it.

All these years... I always thought I was alone.

text.content:
Chen Nian froze for a moment, then her eyes grew moist as she softly called out.

"Brother."

This single "brother" seemed to traverse over a decade of time, finally arriving where it was meant to be.

Chen Ji smiled.

It was the first time in Chen Nian's memory that her brother smiled so easily. Not the usual cold curve of his lips, but a genuine, heartfelt笑意.

Moonlight fell, stretching their shadows long.

In the night wind, the Tianji Record Fragment faintly shimmered, as if witnessing this moment too.

The prelude to the three bloodlines reuniting officially began.

And that half-burned sentence—the true cost of the Heavenly Fate Lock—would, at some future moment, reveal its cruelest truth.
